Socket data, motion pivots, mesh partition names, materials and image payloads remain equal.

action: Inspect matched baseline and preserved radial32 at chase, close, top and side across all tiers
observation: The 24-image comparison retains the lopsided cargo-and-turret silhouette, cockpit ribs, patches, nozzle shapes and livery rings. Close/top/side target draw observations are 30/30/27 for both baseline and candidate. Lower tiers in both show a triangular gold cargo-lid corner and broader gold highlights on the gun arm; these are existing decimation/normal or material-boundary defects rather than a radial32-only regression.
decision: Keep radial32 as the conservative geometry candidate. Investigate the visible lower-tier shading defect separately; do not infer reduced draws or FPS.
next: Compare native normal transfer and material-boundary-preserving decimation.

action: Push visible loft sampling to 24 while preserving collision and motion partitions
observation: The native radial24 build reduces visible triangles to 27372/10440/4384 and source bytes to 1712212/826528/533156. Per-tier baseline collider faces, sockets, pivot data, material JSON, image payloads and mesh partitions remain equal.

action: Transfer full-detail corner normals onto reduced LOD meshes and inspect the result
observation: Native Blender DATA_TRANSFER preserves the baseline corner-normal field on the reduced geometry. The fully drawn LOD1 reverse capture still shows the large triangular gold cargo corner and broad gun-arm highlight, so normal transfer alone does not remove the defect. Re-baked motion banks retain identical clips, events, bindings and fps; only the source hash changes as expected.
decision: Reject normal transfer alone as the shading fix. Test decimation after material separation, since collapsing across the painted boundaries is still a plausible cause.
next: Inspect the material-boundary candidate; retain unchanged canonical assets until a visible improvement exists.
evidenceScope: Current isolated LOD1 picture with 30 observed target draws, plus native source motion-bank comparison.
performance: The first refinement timing batch contains incomplete first frames and order drift. Do not use it as evidence of speedup.

action: Author physical mining and nozzle trail socket pins and resolve their rest-pose contract
observation: The baseline mining anchor is about 1.27 source metres from the authored drill tip; port/starboard trail anchors are about 1.25 metres inboard of their nozzle stations. The scratch socket candidate pins mining to glTF [9.6,-0.58,0], main trail to [-8.4,0.1,0], and side trails to [-9.1,0.05,+/-2.15]. Export preserves these coordinates within float tolerance and leaves per-tier collision, mesh partitions, material/image data and motion bank content unchanged except the necessary source hash.
decision: Keep socket correction separate from the conservative geometry optimization. Root-level sockets still do not inherit MOTION_HULL_CORE; actual moving trail/mining alignment remains a release condition, not a claim from static previews.
next: Observe idle, boost, turning and mining on an actual Drifter instance; if visual detachment is present, coordinate an opt-in native socket motion-parent contract with the exporter owner.
evidenceScope: Native authoring and exported rest-pose data. File previews flatten motion and omit socket empties; diagnostic overlay attempts are not counted as actual VFX or motion acceptance.
performance: No additional visible geometry or image payload is introduced by the socket pins. Runtime performance unmeasured.

action: Inspect the aggressive radial24 candidate with all target draws present across three tiers
observation: The final matched close and inspect pictures retain the lopsided silhouette, gun barrels, crane, patches and nozzle forms at all tiers. No obvious new silhouette break appears at 24 circumference samples. The existing lower-tier triangular gold cargo corner and broad gun-arm highlight remain. Every accepted frame observed 30/30/27 target draws by tier.
decision: Radial24 remains a viable geometry-saving branch but does not address the visible lower-tier boundary defect. Select the corrected radial32 boundary candidate for the current production proposal; combining 24 samples with that fix remains a separate unreviewed candidate.
next: Review material-separated decimation against the same baseline and finalize the scoped production plan.
evidenceScope: Current isolated source GLB pictures through the game renderer; all expected target draws present. No ordinary-play or release-package acceptance.
performance: Visible triangles 27372/10440/4384; accepted target draws unchanged at 30/30/27. No accepted frame-time or FPS gain.

action: Decimate within material boundaries and inspect the resulting lower-tier repair
observation: Separating material groups before native Blender collapse decimation, then transferring reference corner normals, removes the large diagonal gold triangle from the cargo-lid end in LOD1/2; the narrow vertical warning/edge treatment survives. The asymmetric silhouette, nozzle forms and attached machinery remain intact. Broad highlight changes on the gun arm and hull still occur between tiers, so this is a specific boundary repair, not elimination of all LOD shading changes.
decision: Select radial32-preserved-boundaries as the independently reviewable production candidate. It supplies a visible LOD improvement plus geometry/resource savings while preserving each baseline collision triangle set, sockets, materials, image payloads, pivots and partition names. Keep socket correction separate.
next: Coordinate native per-tier collider data and opt-in material-first LOD policy with the Forge owner, then publish only after required release/wreck-fit/live-route checks.
evidenceScope: Native Blender candidate, exact source contract checks, and complete-draw live-render static comparisons. No canonical publication or moving gameplay acceptance.
performance: Visible triangles 38798/15010/6440 -> 30134/11528/4863. Source bytes 2231560/1030184/630860 -> 1837504/881100/565212. Full target draws remain 30/30/27. Frame-time benefit unaccepted.

action: Compare native rebuild precision and inspect the matched all-tier renderer batch
observation: Position-first correspondence separates packing differences from actual errors: position drift reaches about 1.41e-5 source units, UV drift 1.85e-6 and normal/tangent drift about 0.0038. Native LOD0/2 pictures look similar; one native LOD1 frame omits emissive bands despite the expected 30 aggregate target draws. The full batch therefore cannot establish visual equivalence. Early failed GLBs were overwritten by a subsequent experiment; the report records capture source hashes and that retention limitation.
decision: Reject the assumption that aggregate target draws certify complete material presentation. Do not use this batch to relax source tolerances or claim speedup.
next: Resolve native reproducibility and renderer readiness before requesting another acceptance capture.
